question.leadin: Name these people who all formulated their own law codes.
question.text: This Athenian created Athens' first constitution, whose harshness gave rise to a word meaning "marked by extreme severity or cruelty."
question.clue: This man was given jurisdiction after Cylon tried to seize power, and the orator Demades joked that this man wrote in blood rather than in ink.

swap.leadin: The Phaistos Disc, an artifact found in one of this civilization's palaces, may represent an undeciphered writing system.
swap.text: Name this ancient civilization from the island of Crete, which also developed the Linear A writing system.
swap.clue: One of this civilization's palaces is where the mysterious Phaistos disc was found.

question.text: The Battle of Aegospotami ended this series of wars, which was named for a league led by Sparta. This war was temporarily ended with the Peace of Nicias [NIH-kee-as].
question.clue: During this conflict, a general noted that "honor is the delight of men when they are old and useless" as part of a set of remarks that are sometimes attributed to his consort.

swap.leadin: Give the following about famously terse replies in history.
swap.text: After subduing Theban and Athenian forces, this Macedonian king and father of Alexander the Great sent an envoy to Sparta, saying "Surrender now, because if we invade, we will kill you and tear down your city." Sparta's one-word reply, "If.", convinced this man to leave Sparta alone.
swap.answerHtml: Philip II of Macedon (prompt on partial answer)
swap.clue: This leader was killed by a man that Cleitarchus claims had been sexually abused by Attalus.

question.text: Xenophon's Hellenica continues Thucydides's History by discussing such later battles as Notium and Aegospotami [ee-gus-pot-uh-my], which were both victories for this Spartan general. Upon the war's conclusion, this man ordered the walls of Athens to be demolished.
question.clue: This beneficiary of Cyrus the Younger's patronage resumed his most famous office after his replacement Callicratidas lost the battle of Arginusae.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Panhellenic games.
swap.text: The Pythian games occurred in this city, which the Greeks believed was the center of the world. This city was the site of a priestess of Apollo, sometimes called the Pythia.
swap.clue: The Siphnian Treasury and Athenian Treasury were built to house votive offerings at this place, which names a set of hymns by Athenaeus and Limenius.

question.text: This city lies on the isthmus that connects the Peloponnesus with the Grecian mainland. Lucius Mummius destroyed the wealthy city-state in 146 BC in the battle of this city.
question.clue: According to Herodotus, this city provided 40 ships at the Battle of Salamis, the second most after Athens.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about an ancient battle.
swap.text: The Persian Wars began because Athens and several other Greek cities supported the revolts in Asia Minor named after this region, which, along with other regions, including Dorus and Caria, was unsatisfied with its tyrants.
swap.clue: The losing side in this conflict was defeated at Lade and supported by Athens, an alliance that prompted the Battle of Marathon when Darius I sent a punitive expedition.

question.text: Ranked number one was this man, victor of Granicus, Issus, Arbela, and Hydaspes before his early death in 323 BCE.
question.clue: A mosaic of this man at Pompeii shows him astride his favorite mount, Bucephalus, a horse that died at the Battle of the Hydaspes.

swap.text: The Bronze Age Collapse ended the use of this written script, the only one in the Mycenaean language that has been deciphered.
swap.clue: This system consists of ninety syllabic signs, all of which correspond to open syllables.

question.leadin: Answer the following about execution methods throughout history.
question.text: Socrates was condemned to die by drinking the toxic juice of this plant.

swap.leadin: The Mysteries at this site were celebrated until 394AD.
swap.text: Name this city north of Athens which was a celebrated site for the worship of Demeter and Persephone.

question.leadin: Answer the following about people named John who opposed the Ottoman Empire.
question.text: Suleiman the Magnificent conquered this island from the Knights of Saint John, or Knights Hospitallers, in 1523, after which Charles V granted the Knights of Saint John control over Malta.
question.clue: After being expelled from Jerusalem in the 14th century, the Knights of St. John made this their base, although were forced to find a new home after it was sacked in 1522 by Suleiman the Magnificent.

swap.text: According to Strabo, slave trading became rife on this island after the Romans captured it from Perseus of Macedon and made it a free port. Athenian executions would not take place until a sacred ship returned to this island.
swap.clue: Dying in this location was prohibited in a ritual purification during the Peloponnesian War.

question.text: This tyrant of Samos was noted by Herodotus for building three great structures - the great Heraion temple, a great mole in the harbour, and a kilometre long underground aqueduct impressively started from both ends at the same time.
question.clue: This ruler patronized the poets Ibycus (IH-bih-kus) and Anacreon (uh-NAH-kree-on), possibly using money gained through rampant piracy, such as when his fleet of 100 penteconters raided Miletus (my-LEE-tus) and Lesbos.

swap.text: The siege of Syracuse began after a power struggle resulting from the death of this ninety-year old tyrant, who had managed to keep Syracuse out of the First Punic War by signing a 263 BC treaty with Rome.
swap.clue: This tyrant ruled Syracuse until his death in 216 BC, when he was succeeded by his grandson Hieronymus.

question.text: This Mycenaean grave site outside Pylos was first excavated by Jack Davis and Sharon Stocker in 2015. It contained an intricately carved depiction of its title figure known as the Pylos Combat Agate ("AGG-it").

swap.text: A feature of the Magonid army was the existence of a small group of elite fighters with this name; this name also belonged to an elite Theban unit.
swap.clue: This group was unusually put on the left side of an army during a battle in which Cleombrotus's army was destroyed by Epaminondas.

question.text: This Milesian was the instigator of the revolt when he led a mutiny against the city's tyrants on the way back from serving in the Persian navy on the advice of his father Histiaeus.
question.clue: This tyrant of Miletus led the Ionian revolt after failing to take Naxos with the Persian satrap Artaphernes. Gorgo, the young daughter of king Cleomenes, convinced her father not to listen to this man.

swap.text: The second incarnation of this confederation had its leader, Aratus, call for Macedonian help in fighting against Sparta and the Aetolian League.
swap.clue: A brief war named for this power took place after the Romans defeated Andriscus in the Fourth Macedonian War.
